# Ludwig Wittgenstein quote sources

9 passages attributed to Ludwig Wittgenstein in this archive, each with the locator that lets you find it in the work itself — and the one thing that most often goes wrong when people quote Wittgenstein.

[Quote source](https://www.philosophydef.com/quote-source) / Ludwig Wittgenstein

How to cite this author, and what circulates under the name that is not theirs to give.

## Sourcing profile

Language of the works

German

Cited here from

The Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus (5.6, 6.52, 6.54, 7) and the Philosophical Investigations (43, 66, 116, 129).

How to cite it

Decimal number for the Tractatus, remark number for the Investigations. Both systems are the books' own and are preserved in every translation — but always name the work, because the two are usually cited by bare number and the numbers overlap.

Where quotations of this author go wrong

Wittgenstein wrote in German and G. E. M. Anscombe translated the Investigations, so the English aphorism is hers as much as his. More importantly the two books contradict one another: quoting the Tractatus and the Investigations in the same list as “Wittgenstein's view” presents a thinker's abandoned position and its refutation as one doctrine.

2 of the passages below have been worked through against the cited edition, with the original-language wording and the circulating variants recorded on their own pages.

## Frequently asked questions

### Where can I check quotations attributed to Ludwig Wittgenstein?

Decimal number for the Tractatus, remark number for the Investigations. Both systems are the books' own and are preserved in every translation — but always name the work, because the two are usually cited by bare number and the numbers overlap. This archive cites Ludwig Wittgenstein from The Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus (5.6, 6.52, 6.54, 7) and the Philosophical Investigations (43, 66, 116, 129). Every passage listed on this page carries that locator, so it can be found in any edition of the work.

### What is the most common mistake when quoting Ludwig Wittgenstein?

Wittgenstein wrote in German and G. E. M. Anscombe translated the Investigations, so the English aphorism is hers as much as his. More importantly the two books contradict one another: quoting the Tractatus and the Investigations in the same list as “Wittgenstein's view” presents a thinker's abandoned position and its refutation as one doctrine.

### What language did Ludwig Wittgenstein write in?

German. Any English sentence you read is a translation, so a complete source names the translator as well as the passage.
